newsitem.title: JAPAN: Price war puts squeeze on Japan gasoline stations.
newsitem.headline: Price war puts squeeze on Japan gasoline stations.

text.p: An increasing number of gasoline stations in Japan are going bankrupt due to a price war triggered by deregulation of oil product imports in April, a private credit research company said on Tuesday.
From January to October this year a total of 22 gasoline stations collapsed with liabilities reaching a combined four billion yen ($36 million), a survey by Teikoku Databank Ltd showed.
In 1995, a total of nine gasoline stations went out of business, Teikoku Databank said.
"With newcomers entering the gasoline retail market, such s major supermarkets, the oil industry is expected to undergo a reorganisation," it said.
"All levels of the industry, from refiners to retailers, are seen poised for a shake-up," it said.

Since liberalistion of gasoline imports, price-cutting competition between gasoline stations has been heightened by new entrants such as supermarkets. Teikoku Databank said it expects the price war to continue into 1997.
Japan has about 59,990 gasoline stations nationwide selling a combined 50 million kilolitres of gasoline a year.
Industry analysts expect the number of gasoline stations to fall drastically in coming years.
The average retail price of gasoline in Japan as of October 10 was 105 yen per litre, according to the private Oil Information Service Centre. In October 1995 it was 112 yen. ($1=111 yen)
